title: Composables: functions that draw, and the ones that should not

videos.script: In Compose, the screen is a function of your data, and this lesson writes the first of those functions. {{draw}} A composable returns nothing. It describes, and Compose draws what it described. The compiler holds you to one rule about who may call it, and you will see it refuse. {{parameters}} Then parameters. A row for one course gets the course and the minutes, and finds nothing for itself. That makes it easy to show with any data. {{previews}} And showing it is the next step: previews, rendered to pictures from a terminal, with no phone and no Studio. One at normal size, one with the font made larger. {{slots}} Then slots, the trick behind almost every Material component: a parameter that is itself a composable. {{effects}} And last, the ones that should not. A composable runs again and again, so a line that saves or counts inside it runs again and again too. A test counts four where you meant one.
